text: Hoeffding's combinatorial central limit theorem (Ann. Math. Statist. 22 (1951)), with permanents of random sign matrices (Tao and Vu, Adv. Math. 220 (2009)). Target: joint equidistribution of the restricted constants of a block, the first step of a reduction of the dense core to a semi-random residual. The characteristic sum is \(\mathbb E\,\omega^{c(\pi)}=\mathrm{perm}(\omega^A)/N!\), with \(\omega=e^{2\pi i/3}\), so equidistribution is an upper bound on a permanent. Where it breaks: Hoeffding gives a Gaussian limit over the reals, not equidistribution modulo 3. Tao and Vu bound permanents of random \(\pm1\) matrices from below (anti-concentration), whereas the step needs upper bounds for structured phase matrices. And joint equidistribution needs every nonzero combination of the block's forms to have dense interaction: an adversary can make the forms share a dense part while their differences are sparse. The tests: sampling at \(N=200\) with 20000 matchings ( constant_equidistribution.json ) gives a total-variation distance from uniform within sampling noise (0.002) for uniform random coefficients and for full-support product statistics, 0.149 for the identity (Poisson(1) mod 3), and a constant for the row-plus-column form. The exact values of \(|\mathrm{perm}(\omega^A)|/N!\) for even \(N=4,\dots,14\) ( permanent_phases.json ) fall to \(6\times10^{-6}\) for random \(A\), converge to \(e^{-3/2}\approx0.223\) for the identity, and equal 1 for row plus column. For product statistics the largest of five samples is non-monotone (0.661, 0.764, 0.661, 0.346, 0.448, 0.185), still comparable to the identity at these sizes. Test. Passed for single forms at large \(N\); inconclusive for product statistics at small \(N\).

text: The Chevalley–Warning and Alon–Füredi degree bounds. A polynomial on \(\mathbb F_q^m\) that is nonzero at one point and vanishes on all others has degree at least \(m(q-1)\). Target: A1, whether conditioning's cost of 2 per form is forced. Where it breaks: on the Boolean cube with PHP's axioms, a weight need not be a function of the forms alone. Restriction weights, and weights that are not products over blocks, escape it. Test. Passed: over \(\mathbb F_3\) the only function vanishing off a point \(v\) is \(c\prod_j(1-(x_j-v_j)^2)\), of degree \(2m\). By the sparse conditioning theorem's top coefficient, the weight has degree exactly \(2q\) whenever the permanent is nonzero. So for flat weights the cost is optimal.

text: Von zur Gathen and Roche, degrees of symmetric Boolean functions (Comput. Complexity 1997). Target: the encoding step of the integrality line. Their bound gives rational degree at least \(m-O(m^{0.525})\) for nonconstant symmetric functions such as \(\mathrm{MOD}_3\) on \(m\) bits. Where it breaks: it bounds exact encodings only; a lift correct only on the points that matter could be lower. Test. Passed: the rational degree of \([\sum_{i\le m}x_i\not\equiv0\bmod3]\), computed by finite differences, is \(m\) for 12 of \(m=1,\dots,15\) and \(m-1\) for \(m=3,9,15\) ( review_tests.json , T1), as the closed form above predicts. The obstruction holds for exact encodings in the cube variables only.

If saturating pairs of members suffices, gluing becomes local again, at the level of pairs. Test. Passed for trees, falsified for cycles. On chains (two shared forms, path nerve) the pair saturations generate the triple's graded ideal in 4 of 4 trials, although every trial had a falling pair. On triangles (cycle nerve) the triple has further falls in 3 of 4 trials: excesses 1, 1 in degrees 5 and 6; 2, 2 in 7 and 8; 3, 6, 3 in 6 to 8.

text: Lefschetz properties of Artinian algebras (Harima, Migliore, Nagel and Watanabe, J. Algebra 262, 2003). For one row sum, row freeness of \(M\) through \(D\) says that \(r\) acts with all Jordan blocks of length 3 in low degrees, a Lefschetz-type condition. Target: A3 and W through global closure gluing. Answers. Lefschetz theory proves such conditions for quotients by general or monomial ideals, and a condition holding in low degrees is untouched by new generators of higher degree. Row freeness of \(Q\) would follow from the base's, if removing \(Q\)'s error set acts like a quotient by an ideal whose new generators start near the fill point. Test. Passed on the 2 × 8 base: all five families have the base's Jordan-type condition (\(\operatorname{Tor}_1=0\)) through degree 3, and lose it only one degree before their own fill.

text: Dade's lemma (E. C. Dade, Ann. of Math. 108, 1978), with Carlson's rank varieties: over \(\overline{\mathbb F}_3\), a module over \(\Lambda\cong\overline{\mathbb F}_3[(\mathbb Z/3)^{m-1}]\) is free iff it is free over \(k[u_\alpha]/(u_\alpha^3)\) for every \(u_\alpha=\sum_i\alpha_ir_i\ne0\). Target: the obstacle. Answers. Purity against all row sums would reduce to single row forms \(u_\alpha\). Modulo one \(u_\alpha\), only shifts inside its span collapse, and lem:column-tensor-exactness gives single-form annihilators, so the adversary's collapse would have to show in one direction. Where it breaks: the record refutes a truncated version for general column tensors in special position (ex:truncated-dade-special-position), and the board's own row sums need their own statement. Test. Passed in the smallest case: on the 3 × 5 base, \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^\Lambda=0,0,0,103\) in degrees 1 to 4. All 14 distinct single directions tried (the 10 points of \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_9)\) and four random directions over \(\mathbb F_{81}\); one point was run twice) give \(0,0,0,43\). So each detects the first non-free degree exactly and none fails earlier (single_direction.m2, base_3x5.txt). The 3 × 6 run exceeded the 600 s limit in Macaulay2 (base_3x6_3x7_timeout.txt).

text: Jordan type and the Lefschetz properties (Harima, Maeno, Morita, Numata, Wachi, Watanabe, The Lefschetz Properties , LNM 2080, 2013; Iarrobino, Macias Marques, McDaniel, Artinian algebras and Jordan type , 2022). Target: obstacle (a). Answers. Freeness of \(\operatorname{gr}F^Q\) over \(\mathbb F_3[u]/(u^3)\) says that multiplication by \(u\) has Jordan type \((3,\dots,3)\), that is, \(u\) and \(u^2\) have maximal rank in the filtered sense. Maximal rank is the property that Lefschetz theory proves for algebras far from any pullback, by degeneration to monomial or torus-fixed algebras and by Hilbert-function arguments. It is a route to row freeness that does not need joint freeness. Test. Passed: prop:spread-family-level-gap is a Jordan-type statement. Its level gap \(H_{Q_0}(d)>H_{Q_1}(d)\) forces a Jordan block of \(r_i\) shorter than 3 in degree about \(e\). The criterion of prop:single-direction-sectors is equality of the level-set Hilbert functions, which is Jordan type \((3^c)\) through \(D-2\). This check shows the translation is consistent with the proved results. It is no evidence yet that Lefschetz methods reach families beyond capacity.

text: Subspace-evasive sets (Dvir and Lovett, Subspace evasive sets, STOC 2012). Target: the survival condition, which asks whether the added cells' coefficient vectors all lie in one proper subspace \(K_0(z)\). Answers. A deterministic set of vectors meeting every subspace in a family of proper subspaces kills every class; for fixed families this is the derandomization of defect decay. Test. Passed, and reduces to linear algebra: a set of vectors lies in no proper subspace exactly when it spans, so the condition is that the relevant forms are independent off the base, the condition found above. It adds no tool for classes on many tops, where spanning fails by dimension.

text: The Tor identity \(\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(A/I,A/J)\cong(I\cap J)/IJ\) and its Mayer–Vietoris use for sums of ideals (D. Eisenbud, Commutative Algebra with a View Toward Algebraic Geometry, Springer, 1995, appendix on Tor). The sequence below is derived directly, without identifying the defect with a Tor group. For a family split as \(F=F_1\sqcup F_2\) with ideals \(I_1,I_2\) in \(A\), sending a syzygy \((a,b)\) to \(\sum_ia_if_i\in I_1\cap I_2\) is onto, with kernel the syzygies of the parts. The cross Koszul pairs map onto \(I_1I_2\). So there is an exact sequence \[\mathrm{Def}(F_1)\oplus\mathrm{Def}(F_2)\to\mathrm{Def}(F)\to\bigl[(I_1\cap I_2)/(I_1I_2)\bigr]_{e+h}\to0.\] Answers. Locality becomes the vanishing of \((I_1\cap I_2)/(I_1I_2)\) through degree \(e+h\) for separated subfamilies, a Tor-independence statement, which Künneth-type freeness arguments can prove over the union of two subfamilies' forms without freeness over the whole family. Adding tops one at a time, the cross term for \(\tau_b\) is \((I_{<b}:\tau_b)\) modulo \(I_{<b}+\operatorname{ann}\tau_b\), the colon form of prop:sequential-freeness: \(x\mapsto x\tau_b\) maps \((I_{<b}:\tau_b)\) onto \(I_{<b}\cap(\tau_b)\) with kernel \(\operatorname{ann}\tau_b\), and carries \(I_{<b}\) onto \(I_{<b}\tau_b\). Test. Passed: for the shared-square circuit split as its first \(r-1\) tops and the last, \(A^2B_r\in I_1\cap I_2\) at degree 3 while \(I_1I_2\) starts at degree 6, giving the one-dimensional defect exactly; and exact additivity in the random and planted families is consistent with every cross term vanishing there (the sequence alone gives only \(\dim\mathrm{Def}(F)\le\dim\mathrm{Def}(F_1)+\dim\mathrm{Def}(F_2)+\dim\) of the cross term).

text: The nerve theorem and the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence for covers (J. Leray, 1950; see A. Björner, Topological methods, in Handbook of Combinatorics, 1995, Theorem 10.6). A cover's local data generate the global data when the cover's intersections are acyclic. Answers. For the cover by satisfiable closed members, a Leray-type acyclicity of their intersections, whose allowed sets are intersections of allowed sets, would give generation. The obstacle becomes a statement about the nerve of the satisfiable clause sets. Test. Passed as consistency: the cover of the \(c=2\) tensor family by its 13 line sets, where generation fails, has as nerve the complex of lines through common members. That nerve is a union of 13 tetrahedra, one per member, glued at single vertices, so it is homotopy equivalent to the incidence graph of \(\mathrm{PG}(2,3)\): 26 vertices, 52 edges, first Betti number \(52-26+1=27\ne0\). Adding the whole family, a satisfiable member, makes the nerve a cone and generation holds.

text: Hakimi's orientation theorem (S. L. Hakimi, On the degrees of the vertices of a directed graph, J. Franklin Inst. 279, 1965). A graph has an orientation with in-degree at most \(c(v)\) at every vertex iff every subgraph has at most \(\sum c(v)\) edges. Target: conj:row-free-subset for families with pairwise couplings. Answers. With \(c(b)\) the number of cylinder directions member \(b\) can absorb, a repair of all pairwise couplings exists iff the local counting condition holds. This replaces the global obstacle by a density count for pairwise couplings. It breaks for couplings that involve three or more members, which are hyperedges. Test. Passed: the star (one member coupled to \(h\) partners) and the triangle (three members pairwise coupled) both satisfy the count with \(c\equiv1\) on the partners. For the triangle the algebra also goes through. Couple members 1 and 2 along \(w_{12},w_{21}\), members 2 and 3 along \(w_{23},w_{32}\), and members 3 and 1 along \(w_{31},w_{13}\), through three distinct rows, with the six directions distinct coordinates. Orient cyclically: member 1 becomes a cylinder along \(w_{12}\), member 2 along \(w_{23}\) and member 3 along \(w_{31}\). Then the value ring is \(T(w_{12},w_{23},w_{31})\otimes N\), with \(N=M_1''\otimes M_2''\otimes M_3''\). The three row directions act as \(\rho_{12}=w_{12}+n_{12}\), \(\rho_{23}=w_{23}+n_{23}\) and \(\rho_{31}=w_{31}+n_{31}\). Here \(n_{12}=w_{21}\) acts on \(M_2''\), \(n_{23}=w_{32}\) on \(M_3''\) and \(n_{31}=w_{13}\) on \(M_1''\); they commute and cube to zero. This is the tensor product, under the primitive coproduct of the three-variable truncated algebra, of its regular module with \(N\), so it is free. The full freeness of the triangle's subset still needs the analogous pullback hypotheses for three members, which are not checked.
